answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3, well away from the central blob.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units carry very large weights confined to the same 3x3 block (rows 1-3, cols 1-3). Pro-large units 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20 and 29 have strong positive weights there (about +40 to +99), and the same units also respond positively to a large central disc. Background or small-blob units 5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27 and 30 have strong negative weights there (about -30 to -98). In layer 2, units u3 and u10 (output weights +67 and +74) take large positive input from the pro-large group and negative input from the other group. Units u0 and u6 (output weights -99 and -93) are wired the opposite way. A bright patch therefore switches on the class-1 pathway and switches off the class-0 pathway, pushing the logit toward 'large blob'.
answer.evidence: In every structured first-layer unit, the 3x3 block at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 holds the largest-magnitude weights in the whole grid. Examples: unit 4 has 93, 98, 98, 94; unit 20 has 81-94; unit 5 has -82 to -98; unit 14 has -77 to -98. The weights around this block are only at noise level, and no other corner shows anything similar. The sign of the patch weights always matches the sign the unit gives to the large-disc pattern. Layer 2 then combines the units consistently: u3 receives about +570 summed weight from the patch-positive units and about -360 from the patch-negative units, and u10 receives about +516 and -320. Both feed the output positively. u0 and u6 have the reverse pattern and feed the output negatively.
answer.main_feature: Blob extent. Pro-large units respond to brightness spread over a wide central disc (roughly rows 5-18, cols 5-18). Small-blob/background units have a negative ring around the centre and positive weights on the dark periphery, so they fire when the bright region stays small.
